initial_plan.can_answer: partly: the data can show annual counts of pedestrians injured and killed in Brooklyn crashes, but cannot establish an exposure-adjusted change in road safety or explain causes
initial_plan.metric: annual number of pedestrians injured and annual number of pedestrians killed
initial_plan.denominator: none for the counts; each crash row contributes its recorded pedestrian injury and fatality counts
initial_plan.population: all police-reported motor vehicle crashes in Brooklyn in each included calendar year
initial_plan.years: 2013 through the latest complete calendar year present in the file
initial_plan.chart_type: stacked annual bar chart (injured and killed shown as separate components)

facts: The file has dated records from 2013-01-01 through 2026-06-11; 2026 is partial, so the final comparison uses 2013-2025.
The file stores borough labels in uppercase; matching after trimming whitespace and ignoring case yields the Brooklyn population.
Among 2,132,218 dated NYC crash rows in 2013-2025, 659,713 (30.9%) have borough missing or unknown and cannot be assigned to Brooklyn; exclude and disclose them.

Within the selected Brooklyn rows in 2013-2025, the pedestrian injury and fatality fields have no missing or negative values. Zero is a valid recorded count, not an unknown/default to discard; keep those rows and count zero as zero.
No crash-date missingness occurs within the selected dated population.
decisions: Exclude rows with missing/unknown borough because they cannot be reliably assigned; disclose the excluded volume.
Retain valid zeros and all selected Brooklyn crash rows.

final_plan.can_answer: partly: shows how recorded pedestrian injuries and deaths changed in Brooklyn crashes, but does not measure risk per pedestrian trip or distance and cannot establish whether overall road safety got better
final_plan.metric: annual count of pedestrians injured and annual count of pedestrians killed, separately summed across Brooklyn crash records
final_plan.denominator: none; these are annual counts, with each crash row contributing its recorded pedestrian counts
final_plan.population: all police-reported motor vehicle crashes assigned to Brooklyn, 2013-2025
final_plan.chart_type: stacked annual bar chart (injured and killed shown as separate components)
final_plan.limitations: Counts describe recorded pedestrian harm in police-reported crashes, not exposure-adjusted risk; 659,713 of 2,132,218 dated NYC crashes in 2013-2025 (30.9%) lack a usable borough and are excluded, and 2026 is partial and excluded.
